modelgate

Native R port of the Python library bdp-model-gate, which is its reference implementation: run automated governance checks on a model before it ships and get one verdict a pipeline can branch on.

Verdict Meaning Exit code
PASS nothing found 0
BLOCKED a blocking check found a problem 1
NEEDS_REVIEW only non-blocking checks found something; a person decides 2 
library(modelgate)
ctx <- gate_context(X = X_val, X_train = X_train)
report <- run_gate(ctx)
report                    # prints the verdict and findings
gate_exit_code(report)    # for CI

Status: pre-alpha. All five validation checks are ported (target_leakage, split_overlap, validation_strategy, feature_contract, feature_drift) plus the framework. Targets bdp-model-gate 0.7.0. See the roadmap below.

Releases take the version number of the bdp-model-gate release whose behaviour they match, so the first release will be 0.7.0.

How “correct” is defined here

The upstream project exists to avoid one failure: a gate that returns a confident, wrong, green number. So the bar for every check is “a test would have noticed if this were wrong”, not “the tests pass”:

  1. Known-answer tests first - inputs whose answer is derivable on paper, asserted exactly (tests/testthat/test-split-overlap.R).
  2. Invariance tests - permute rows, scramble row names, reorder columns.
  3. Every skip path asserted on its reason string. A check that cannot answer returns NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason, never a plausible number.
  4. Parity with the Python library (test-parity.R) as a second layer, from fixtures made by tools/make_parity_fixtures.py. The oracle has been wrong before, so a disagreement is a question, not automatically an R bug.
  5. Use run_gate_strict() (in tests/testthat/helper-guard.R) in tests, not run_gate(). The gate turns an error inside a check into a blocking CHECK_ERROR result, so length(results) > 0 passes on a crashed check.

Deliberate differences from upstream

  • Numbers match by value: an integer column in one frame and a double column in the other still overlap. Upstream 0.7.0 hashes by dtype, so X = data.frame(a = 1:5) against X_train holding 1.0 ... 5.0 reports 0 of 5 overlapping there. Reported upstream as vanjy-eng/model-gate#31; the repro is in tools/.
  • feature_drift treats a training column whose values are all identical as constant and skips it. Upstream tests the standard deviation against zero, which rounding defeats for values such as 0.1: a 0.001 change then reports a standardised mean shift of about 7e13. Repro in tools/upstream_constant_drift_repro.py.
  • feature_drift matches category levels by label. When a column holds numbers in one frame and text in the other, upstream (on pandas 2.x) looks levels up by position and reports a wrong distance, such as 0.75 where it should be 1. Repro in tools/upstream_mixed_type_tvd_repro.py.
  • feature_contract takes the expected columns from expected_features, then from X_train. Upstream can also read them from scikit-learn, LightGBM and XGBoost model objects; R models record their columns in different ways, so pass expected_features when the training frame is not to hand.
  • target_leakage covers binary and continuous targets; a multiclass target is skipped with a reason for now. Rows with a missing y_true are left out and counted in the message. Upstream counts them as positives on a binary target, and on a continuous one returns OK with a model power of NaN, missing the leak. Repro in tools/upstream_leakage_missing_target_repro.py.
  • ASCII hyphens instead of em dashes in message text.
